name: Fever in Adults (including suspected malaria)
source_guidance: Adapted from WHO Guidelines for Malaria (danger signs of severe malaria and test-before-treat), the Nigeria National Malaria Treatment Guidelines, and NHS guidance on fever and sepsis.

questions.text: Is the person unconscious, very hard to wake, confused, or having fits?
Is the person too weak to sit, stand, or walk without help?
Is there difficulty breathing, or a stiff neck with severe headache?
Is there unusual bleeding, a rash that does not fade when a glass is pressed on it, or very dark urine or little or no urine?
Is the person pregnant, or vomiting everything so they cannot keep fluids or medicine down?
Are the eyes or skin yellow?
Has the fever lasted more than three days, or come back after malaria treatment?
Has the person not yet had a malaria test for this fever?

emergency: Call 112 now, or get to the nearest hospital emergency department immediately.
These are danger signs of severe malaria or another serious infection and need hospital treatment now.
Lay the person on their side if drowsy or fitting. Do not put anything in their mouth during a fit.
Do not drive yourself. Ask someone to take you, or wait for the ambulance.
urgent: Go to a hospital, clinic, or primary health centre today.
Ask for a malaria test (rapid diagnostic test) before any malaria treatment.
Drink fluids in small, frequent sips if able.
Call 112 if the person becomes confused, very weak, or has fits.
self_care: The person has a fever with no danger signs and has already tested negative for malaria.
Rest and drink plenty of fluids.
Paracetamol can be taken as directed on the pack.
Sleep under an insecticide-treated mosquito net.
Call back if the fever lasts more than three days or any danger sign appears.
